speaker: Elder Maren
before: Bars, and white coats, and 'again.' So that is where they had you, all those years.
after: Bars, and white coats, and 'again.' So that is where you were kept, all those years. I'm sorry, dearie. Nobody should ever be anyone's 'Subject'.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: The way you said that... I taught the royal children at the castle once, and there was a boy who asked his questions just that way. For a moment I thought... No. That boy is ten years dead, and I'm a foolish old tortoise.
after: I'll be honest with you. A Path-walker strong enough to free a zone walks out of my cave remembering nothing, or saying so. I didn't know what to make of you, and I wasn't sure I could trust you.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: You've earned some truth in return: I'm not only an old tortoise who bakes. There's a resistance in this kingdom, and I'm its contact here in {town}. A woman called Wren leads it, from a hideout inside the Capital itself.
after: But whatever you are, you're helping us, and that counts for more than a name. So, some truth in return: there's a resistance in this kingdom, and I'm its contact in {town}. A woman called Wren leads it, from inside the Capital.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I wasn't sure of you before, and I'm sorry for that. I'm sure of you now, or near enough, and there aren't many people I would say that about.
after: What frightens me is the day your memories come back. You may find you had reasons to side with the crown, or none to stay here. When that day comes, I hope you'll still choose to help us.

speaker: The Rescuer
before: Go now, and don't stop for anything. I'll draw them off the other way, and once I'm clear of them, I'll find you. I always do.
after: Go now, and don't stop for anything. I'll draw them off the other way, and once I'm clear of them and it's safe, I'll come and find you. Trust me that far.

speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
before: I won't come into town, though. The old woman with the shell looks at me as if I owe her something, and she's probably right.
after: I won't come into town, though. I can't risk being seen.

speaker: (narration)
before: The hooded figure is back at the cave mouth, this time with two cups of something hot. She hands you one without asking whether you want it.
after: The hooded figure is back at the cave mouth, pacing. She keeps glancing at the treeline and the road, and only stops when she sees that it's you.

speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
before: Drink your tea. It's for the shaking.
after: Never mind that. Did anyone follow you? Patrols have been through these woods twice since this morning, and they were looking hard.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Great news, citizens! The D.N.A. has been freed, a change His Perfection fully supports and in fact arranged!
after: Great news, citizens! The D.N.A. is undergoing a leadership transition, which His Perfection fully supports and, in a very real sense, arranged!

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Attention, citizens. (a cough) The weather is no longer approved; it is just weather, and it seems to be managing on its own.
after: Attention, citizens. (a cough) The weather has been deregulated, a bold reform this office has always quietly championed. It seems to be managing on its own.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: So please do whatever you like today. I have nothing further to announce, and I find, rather to my surprise, that I do not mind.
after: So please do whatever you like today. That is the new official position, and I would like it on the record that I held it first.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Attention, citizens. He was afraid, and we were afraid of him. Please be gentle with yourselves.
after: Attention, citizens. Following a leadership transition, nobody is watching you any more. This office fully supports the transition, effective retroactively.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Attention, citizens. All is not well. I am told that I may say so now. All is not well yet, but it is getting better.
after: Attention, citizens. All is well, and getting weller. I am told that is not a word. This office has approved it anyway.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: It is a great deal of work, and I notice it is mostly you who are doing it. Thank you. This has been... well. This has been Percival.
after: There is a great deal of work to do, and you are doing most of it, which this office fully supports and will be issuing certificates for. This has been Percival.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Attention, citizens. The Wrinkles were real all along, and they kept the true record. Please thank them.
after: Attention, citizens. The Wrinkles have been reclassified as a heritage archive, which this office has always privately valued. Please thank them.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: 'CLOSED UNTIL TWO ZONES ARE FREE. {villain} TOOK MY CAULDRON. I AM BREWING IN THE SINK. THE SINK IS COPING. - A.'
after: 'CLOSED FOR INVENTORY. AND FOR REASONS. {villain} TOOK MY CAULDRON, SO I AM BREWING IN THE SINK. DO COME BACK LATER, DEAR. - A.'

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: With two zones free, a cauldron bubbles to life in {town}, and Auntie Alembic's is open! Bring your essence and your courage, and it wouldn't hurt to bring a fire blanket.
after: With a zone free, a cauldron bubbles to life in {town}, and Auntie Alembic's is open! Bring your essence and your courage, and it wouldn't hurt to bring a fire blanket.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: When you collect more copies of a card than you can carry, dear heart, the extras boil down into essence of that card's Path. Nothing goes to waste here, which is how I like a kitchen and a kingdom.
after: When you collect a fourth copy of a card, dear heart, it boils down into essence of that card's Path. Nothing goes to waste here, which is how I like a kitchen and a kingdom.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: Bring me six essence each of two Paths, plus 100 gold, and I'll brew you a card of both. The cauldron picks which card, and now and then it's on fire. I only take what the brew needs; the rest stays in your jars.
after: Bring me six essence each of two Paths, plus 40 gold, and I'll brew you a card of both. The cauldron picks which card, and now and then it's on fire. The rest stays in your jars.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: Your jars hold eighteen of a Path. Anything past that drifts off as steam, and then my ceiling turns a new colour and I have to pretend I meant it.
after: Your jars hold eighteen of a Path. Past that, the extras drift off as steam, and then my ceiling turns a new colour and I have to pretend I meant it.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: Six essence each of two Paths and 100 gold, dear heart, and the cauldron does the rest. Do lower your voice near the red flask, though, because it takes things very personally.
after: Six essence each of two Paths and 40 gold, dear heart, and the cauldron does the rest. Do lower your voice near the red flask, though, because it takes things very personally.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: Oh, and here, before I drift off and forget: a starter jar of every Path, six of each, which is enough for one brew of any two. Please don't drink it, dear heart. People do drink it.
after: And here, before I forget: a starter jar of every Path, six of each. That's two brews: click two jars, then Craft, then the other two. Please don't drink it, dear heart. People do.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Two zones free, and Auntie Alembic has opened the Alchemist's on the square. She brews cards from two Paths at once, if you can stand all the steam.
after: Two zones free. Have you been to Auntie Alembic's yet? She brews cards of two Paths at once, if you can stand all the steam.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: SINCE YOU FREED A ZONE, THE RING IS OPEN! (normal voice) It's battles and puzzles, tiers one to three, and there are prizes for you: ring-exclusive gear, gold and essence.
after: WITH {villain}'S GUARDS GONE FROM CROSSPATH, THE RING IS OPEN AGAIN! (normal voice) He needs his soldiers elsewhere these days, it seems. His grip on this corner has slipped, and the sand is ours.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: FIRST CLEARS PAY OUT, AND REPEATS ARE FOR GLORY! (normal voice) And for snacks, I should say. I brought snacks, and there are plenty to go round.
after: EVERY WIN PAYS GOLD AND A PACK, AND EVERY TIER HAS ITS PRIZE! (normal voice) Bronze to Diamond, battles and puzzles. Beat a whole tier and the next one opens. I brought snacks.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: VICTORY ON THE SAND, AND THE PRIZE IS YOURS! (normal voice) Do mind your head on the way up to collect it, because the ceiling doesn't celebrate with the rest of us.
after: VICTORY ON THE SAND, AND THE SPOILS ARE YOURS! (normal voice) Do mind your head on the way up to collect them, because the ceiling doesn't celebrate with the rest of us.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: The gates are chained until the first zone is free.
after: Chained shut by order of {villain_title}. Come back once his guards have moved on.
